title.children: EXIT-CVD: Transforming Cardiovascular Care Across Europe

blocks.subtitle: A five-year research project uniting 42 partners across 17 countries to help cardiac patients avoid deterioration through early, personalised interventions delivered across the cardiac care journey.

blocks.title: About EXIT-CVD
blocks.content:
The EXIT-CVD research consortium, co-funded by the European Union Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) and industry partners, aims to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated.
It identifies and acts on three key exit points along the cardiac care journey:
  1. Early Exit - Preventing disease before it develops through digital monitoring and early detection
  2. Mid Exit - Reversing disease progression through personalised risk assessment and targeted interventions
  3. Late Exit - Halting progression in advanced stages with advanced therapies to support recovery

Led by the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG) and Philips, the consortium brings together 42 public and private partners across 17 countries to conduct 22 clinical studies involving over 14,000 patients.

content.title: Powered by Onsentia & RADAR-base
content.content:
Onsentia powers the digital data collection and remote monitoring infrastructure for EXIT-CVD using the open-source RADAR-base platform.
The platform combines: - Active monitoring (aRMT) - Patient-reported outcome questionnaires - Passive monitoring (pRMT) - Broad passive sensor and wearable data collection - Huawei D3 Watch - Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring via integrated oscillometric wrist BP cuff
This enables multi-source, scalable, real-time remote monitoring and data integration across clinical trials.

content.title: COMPASS Study
content.content:
Led by King's College London (KCL) / GSTT, the COMPASS study brings together unique technological capabilities from several partners.
Huawei Health provides ambulatory blood pressure monitoring via its D3 Watch, with a novel integrated oscillometric wrist BP cuff. Onsentia's decentralised remote monitoring platform collects data from the Huawei D3 Watch. MEGI provides an AI-powered digital health app for personalised cardiovascular assessments, and CogStack assists in identifying participants from medical records.

content.title: EMPOWER-BP Study
content.content:
UMC Utrecht, together with Universita' Di Pavia, Politecnico Di Milano, and Stichting Vrouwenhart, the EMPOWER-BP study utilises a citizen science approach.
Participants are recruited to Onsentia's platform via remote self-enrolment through social media and the Huawei D3 Watch wearable. This study seeks to engage patients directly in their health management, enhancing adherence and reducing healthcare costs.

blocks.title: Innovation That Reaches Everyone
blocks.content:
New diagnostics and digital tools often reach well-resourced populations first, widening gaps in access and outcomes. EXIT-CVD embeds implementation science and equity-by-design principles to ensure solutions are scalable, sustainable, and accessible to all relevant populations, including those historically underserved.
A digitally enabled, FAIR-compliant data platform aligned with the European Health Data Space (EHDS) supports the integration, evaluation, and real-world scalability of the project's innovations.

blocks.title: What Will I Have To Do?

items.title: 1. Check eligibility and provide consent
items.content: Complete a brief eligibility check to confirm you can take part, then read the Participant Information Sheet and sign an electronic consent form.

items.title: 2. Set up your study account
items.content: Create an account with your email address and a password. You will need to verify your email before you can proceed.

items.title: 3. Connect your devices
items.content: Connect the Huawei D3 Watch for blood pressure and health monitoring, install the RADAR Active App (aRMT) for questionnaires, and the RADAR Passive App (pRMT) for passive data collection.

items.title: 4. Participate in monitoring
items.content: Wear the Huawei D3 Watch as instructed, complete regular questionnaires via the Active App, and keep the Passive App running on your smartphone.
